- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–15% relative to historical mean.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 3–8% to align with recent trend momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to recent high prices; apply mean reversion bias: if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20%.
- Lagged forecasts consistently underestimate; shift forecast horizon forward by 1–2 days for short-term (1–7 day) predictions.
- After a price spike, forecast should not overshoot by more than 10% above the peak; cap forecast at 1.1x peak value.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers; cap forecast at ±15% of 30-day moving average to prevent volatility overestimation.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid runaway bias.
